correctness.rationale: PASS. Symmetrization of squared Euclidean distances (not of maps) preserves conditional negativity and the noncontracting C^2 interval. Incidence-space Fourier decomposition of Johnson-scheme adjacency matrices yields the three nontrivial eigenvalue rows (-L,(n-4)(n-9)/2,2n-9), (n-5,11-2n,n-7),(-1,3,-3), L=binom(n-4,2). The W1 inequality gives sharp lower bound for n>=9; explicit x=(4(1-1/L),4,4) obeys all three. For n=8, 3*W1+2*W3 gives x0>=3x2/4, and (3,5,4) meets sharpness. Equality of orbit averages at bounding values pins every pair distance for n>=10; at n=8 orbit x1=5 differs from x2=4, forcing nonfaithfulness. Independent exact finite differences reproduced the eigenvalue rows for n=8..40 and checked the claimed pointwise optimal squared-distance patterns including n=9 alternative.

final_claim: For n>=8, KG(n,3) has least real Hilbert distortion sqrt(3) at n=8 and 2sqrt(1-1/binom(n-4,2)) for n>=9. The n=8 optimum is necessarily nonfaithful, n=9 has faithful and nonfaithful optima, and n>=10 all normalized optimal distance patterns are identical.
